source.title: DRIFT: Data Reduction via Informative Feature Transformation- Generalization Begins Before Deep Learning starts

record.tranche_reason: The study varies batch size and reports effects on convergence and generalization, refining the claim that large batches worsen held-out performance: some reported instability occurs at small batch sizes, and DRIFT is described as stable across batch sizes. It does not report fixed-epoch comparisons.
record.gate_note: The study's own batch-size comparisons bear on V5. Other results about mode count, resolution, and DRIFT versus PCA or the full-input network do not test the listed versions. Referenced prior-work findings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study varies batch size, but does not establish fixed epoch budgets or report a matched large-versus-small-batch held-out penalty. Its principal findings concern preprocessing performance and convergence stability. These do not test V5 as stated, and no other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that DRIFT improves training stability and training-test alignment relative to PCA and full-input models, with reduced sensitivity to batch size on MNIST and CIFAR100. This is their interpretation, not evidence establishing V5's fixed-epoch comparison.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies physics-inspired feature preprocessing and compares DRIFT, PCA, and full-input feedforward networks; it does not reproduce the original batch-size methods or state fixed epoch budgets.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size is varied; the reported effects differ by representation and model. Mode count and input resolution are also varied, but those results do not test a listed claim version.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, the Full model's training loss and convergence improve as batch size increases; on CIFAR100, PCA and Full models diverge with batch size 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size affects optimization stability in these feedforward image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: DRIFT is described as relatively insensitive to batch size and as maintaining stable training and generalization across tested conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vibrational-mode preprocessing can improve robustness to batch-size changes relative to PCA and full-pixel inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: The Full model has reduced generalization at batch size 128 on CIFAR100, without an explicit held-out comparison against batch size 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The full-input classifier generalizes poorly in this particular configuration.

record.problems: Results on batch-size effects are qualitative descriptions of figures without reported numerical values or uncertainty. The study does not state that training epoch budgets are fixed. The text says the CIFAR100 Figure 7 network has 32 hidden units, while its caption says '32-layer hidden architecture.'
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the same batch-size comparisons were needed; non-batch-size results do not bear on the tested version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label held-out generalization.
Test error when hidden-layer width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers and tuning-dependent differences.
Held-out penalties from larger batches under fixed epoch budgets, and whether adapted training recipes remove those penalties.
Effects of dropout and its interaction with dataset size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance ranking generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V5 verdicts. Neither small-batch instability nor an unspecified training budget supports a challenge or scope limitation for that version. Figure plots are not readable in the supplied text, so numerical endpoint comparisons and training budgets cannot be recovered.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Whether large batches hurt under fixed epoch budgets; longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, normalization, or regularization adaptations; language models.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures tracking the generalization gap.

rows.subject: Full model (baseline NN using all original input features)
rows.operation_detail: Compared batch sizes with 30 modes in the MNIST experiment.
rows.baseline: Batch sizes 32 and 256: loss decreases and convergence improves as batch size increases.
rows.value: Batch size 2: notably high training loss and significant instability in convergence.
rows.note: Qualitative result; no values transcribed from the figure.
rows.check: Training loss and convergence instability do not measure V5's held-out performance penalty. Better optimization with larger batches is not a reversal of V5. The Full model uses all pixels; 30 modes applies to the reduced-input comparators.

rows.subject: DRIFT model
rows.operation_detail: Compared batch sizes with 30 modes in the MNIST experiment.
rows.baseline: DRIFT performance at other tested batch sizes; exact values not stated.
rows.value: The text says DRIFT maintains smooth convergence and competitive test accuracy even at batch size 2, and that batch-size changes have minimal impact.
rows.note: The text describes relative stability, not a numerical train-test gap or fixed-epoch comparison.
rows.check: Qualitative batch-size robustness is reported, but fixed epoch budgets and a matched held-out comparison are not established. This cannot justify a partial V5 effect.

rows.subject: Full model
rows.operation_detail: Compared batch sizes with 80 input modes and 32 hidden units in the CIFAR100 experiment.
rows.baseline: Batch size 2 condition; exact values not stated.
rows.value: At batch size 128, the Full model suffers from reduced generalization, as described in the text.
rows.note: The text does not quantify the difference or state that epoch budgets were fixed.
rows.check: Reduced generalization at batch size 128 is not explicitly a decline relative to batch size 2; the stated baseline is unsupported. The Full model uses all pixels, not 80 modes. Fixed epoch budgets are unspecified.

rows.subject: DRIFT model
rows.operation_detail: Compared batch sizes with 80 input modes and 32 hidden units in the CIFAR100 experiment.
rows.baseline: DRIFT at the other tested batch size; exact values not stated.
rows.value: The text says DRIFT maintains stable convergence and generalization under batch size 2 and shows stable trajectories at batch size 128.
rows.note: The text describes qualitative behavior, not a numerical gap or fixed-epoch comparison.
rows.check: Stable trajectories at both batch sizes do not establish their relative held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets. The text says 32 hidden units, while the caption inconsistently describes 32 layers.

rows.subject: PCA-based model
rows.operation_detail: Compared batch sizes with 80 input modes and 32 hidden units in the CIFAR100 experiment.
rows.baseline: Batch size 128 condition; exact values not stated.
rows.value: The text says PCA begins to diverge after some training iterations at batch size 2; the batch size 128 trajectory is described as stable.
rows.note: Qualitative result; no values transcribed from the figure.
rows.check: Small-batch divergence versus large-batch stability concerns optimization reliability; it does not establish a reversal of the fixed-epoch held-out penalty in V5.

rows.subject: Full model
rows.operation_detail: Compared batch sizes with 80 input modes and 32 hidden units in the CIFAR100 experiment.
rows.baseline: Batch size 128 condition; exact values not stated.
rows.value: The text says the Full model begins to diverge after some training iterations at batch size 2; at batch size 128 it suffers from reduced generalization.
rows.note: The described outcomes at the two batch sizes concern different measures, so their comparison does not determine the direction of a single measure.
rows.check: Small-batch divergence and large-batch reduced generalization are different outcomes, without a matched held-out comparison. The Full model uses all pixels, not 80 modes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
